land.text: 'the area east of the Lauwers', held by the Franks since 785 and drawn as Frankish by Cliopatria in 788-792

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Frankish shape holds these 33 cells in 788-792 and from 800 and leaves them out in 793-799, when the Frisians row exists. The free Frisian state east of the Lauwers is the frisia dossier (ends 785).

land.text: the same 33 cells, Frankish again from 800 in Cliopatria

successors.note: No page opened dates the return.

keyframe_review.note: 8,792 km2, 793-799: 33 cells (Groningen 10 of 10, Niedersachsen 19, Friesland 2, Drenthe 1), the same outline as Cliopatria's Magna Frisia (741-771) and the land east of the Lauwers. Unverified: the Frisia page has 'Frankish troops conquered the area east of the Lauwers in 785' and the Frisians page the 734 subjugation, and neither page says a word of 793-799; a free Frisian state in these years rests on Cliopatria alone. Cliopatria's Frankish shape leaves the cells out exactly in 793-799. Neither page gives an area.

region.text: the Frisian land east of the Lauwers, in Cliopatria's Frisians row

ledger.note: 793: Cliopatria draws the Frisian land east of the Lauwers as its own row. Page silent: the Frisia page ends the Frisian Realm 'in 734 at the Battle of the Boarn' and has the Franks conquer 'the area east of the Lauwers in 785'; the Frisians page has nothing for 793-799. The year is Cliopatria's, bridging a silence.

region.text: the Frisian land east of the Lauwers

ledger.note: 799: Cliopatria's Frisians row ends and its Frankish shape holds the land again from 800. Page silent about 799; the Frisia page has only the 785 conquest, and the later Frisian 'freedom' under the emperor is undated on the Frisians page.

wars.name: Frankish conquest of Frisia

wars.outcome: The Franks defeated the Frisians at the Boarn in 734 ('the Frankish Empire eventually subjugated Frisia in 734') and 'Frankish troops conquered the area east of the Lauwers in 785, after Charlemagne defeated the Saxon leader Widukind'.
wars.note: Before this state's life; kept because it is the last dated event on the pages. The Frisians page puts Boniface's death near Dokkum in 754 as a sign that the north was not yet fully Frankish.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary; the Lauwers is the only line named, as the old west limit of the land.

sources.title: Frisians

sources.title: Frisia
sources.note: Frisian Realm 650-734, Boarn 734, the Franks east of the Lauwers 785, Vikings 840s-920; nothing for 793-799.

notes: Frisians (eu-07-d), two pages of two budgeted (Frisians, Frisia). Both pages are silent on 793-799: no rising, no independence, no ruler, no seat. Cliopatria's row is the 33-cell land east of the Lauwers (the same outline as Magna Frisia 741-771 and Frisia 783-787), left out of its Kingdom of the Franks shape exactly in 793-799. What the pages do say: the Frisian Realm (650-734) had 'its centre of power in the city of Utrecht' and fell 'in 734 at the Battle of the Boarn'; 'Frankish troops conquered the area east of the Lauwers in 785'; the coast was partly occupied by Danish Vikings from the 840s until 885-920. So the pages show a Frankish land in 793-799, and the verdict ok is a deliberate 'unverified': if the eu-06/eu-07 reviewers believe in a Saxon-Frisian rising of 793 they need a page for it (the Saxon Wars page was not opened in this batch), and if not, this row should be dropped and the land left to the Franks, with the Frankish dossier covering 793-799. Not settled. No capital: none on the pages for 793-799 (empty list). The Frisia page's Lex Frisionum date is 'late eighth century', not 802. Counterpart kingdom-of-the-franks is the Cliopatria row (462-849); the frisia and magna-frisia dossiers (eu-06, eu-07-c) carry the earlier free Frisia. No gazetteer names needed.
